findings.title: Arguments are rounded to `prec` bits before the guard bits apply, so large irrational `h` returns wrong digits.
findings.body: `h` and `a` are converted with `_to_mpmath(prec)`, outside `workprec(prec + 10)`, so the guard bits never reach the inputs. The integrand is `exp(-h²(1+t²)/2)`, which means a relative error δ in `h` becomes a relative error of about `h²·δ` in T. For an irrational `h` such as `100*sqrt(2)`, `h²` is about 2·10⁴ (~15 bits), more than the 10 guard bits, so the trailing digits of the result are wrong but get reported as accurate. That breaks the `Add` cancellation retries this change is meant to support. Fix: convert the arguments at a higher precision that grows with `h`, e.g. `prec + 10 + bitcount(|h|²)`, inside the `workprec` block.

held.title: The `mpmath.quad` error estimate is never checked, so an inaccurate quadrature is returned at full claimed precision.
held.body: `mpmath.quad` never raises when tanh-sinh fails to converge. It just returns its best estimate. The result goes straight to `Expr._from_mpmath(result, prec)` and is reported as accurate to `prec` bits. This can go wrong when `|h|` is large and `a` is far from 0 (e.g. `owens_t(40, 1e6)`), because the integrand is a narrow peak of width about 1/|h| at the start of a very long interval, and when `a` is complex with a large modulus. In those cases the result can carry far fewer correct bits than claimed, and `Add` uses it without knowing. The old `Integral.evalf` path tracked quadrature accuracy. Fix: call `mpmath.quad(..., error=True)` and return `None` (or retry at higher precision) when the error is too large. Also consider splitting the interval at about `min(|a|, c/|h|)` so the peak gets its own subinterval.
